name: Udawalawe National Park
description: Udawalawe National Park, a protected area in Ratnapura, Sri Lanka, offers visitors opportunities to observe wildlife such as elephants, leopards, and various bird species. Established in 1972 following the construction of a dam, the park was created to provide a habitat for these animals and protect their natural environment. Notable events include the successful relocation of several elephant herds, a feat that showcases the park's commitment to conservation. Visitors can enjoy guided nature walks and safaris to witness the diverse flora and fauna in their natural setting.
mobile_signal: Good near entrance and Elephant Transit Home
activities: Elephant watching, bird watching, nature walks
ticket_price: USD 42.5 (foreign adult) including taxes; LKR ~60 (local adult)
wheelchair_access: elephant transit home viewing deck is wheelchair accessible
monsoon_note: Some interior tracks flood during NE monsoon (Oct-Jan); reservoir levels rise, improving elephant sightings near shoreline

name: Sinharaja Forest Reserve
description: Sinharaja Forest Reserve, a UNESCO World Heritage site in Ratnapura, Sri Lanka, is a vital sanctuary for over 200 species of birds and numerous other wildlife. This ancient forest, once part of King Mahinda's Buddhist mission, plays a crucial role in the island's biodiversity. It was declared a national heritage area in 1978, safeguarding the unique ecosystem from deforestation. Visitors can explore the reserve through guided treks, bird watching tours, and nature photography sessions, experiencing the natural beauty and tranquility of this irreplaceable tropical rainforest.
activities: Bird watching, nature photography, jungle trekking
ticket_price: LKR 1000 (local adult) approx; USD 20-25 (foreign adult) approx including guide fee
food_nearby: limited small shops/guesthouses near kudawa entrance

name: Peak Wilderness Sanctuary
description: Peak Wilderness Sanctuary, located in Ratnapura, Sri Lanka, is a protected area known for its diverse flora and fauna. Established as a sanctuary in 1982, it encompasses over 4,000 hectares of land. Visitors can explore its trails on foot, take stunning photographs, and engage in meditation retreats. The sanctuary plays a crucial role in conserving local ecosystems and biodiversity. It's also significant for its historical importance, having been used by the ancient Sigiriya civilization. Its lush green landscapes and rich wildlife make it a popular destination for nature enthusiasts and those seeking tranquility.
